NKJV.1: It came to pass at that time that Judah departed from his brothers, and visited a certain Adullamite whose name was Hirah.
NKJV.2: And Judah saw there a daughter of a certain Canaanite whose name was Shua, and he married her and went in to her.
NKJV.3: So she conceived and bore a son, and he called his name Er.
NKJV.4: She conceived again and bore a son, and she called his name Onan.
NKJV.5: And she conceived yet again and bore a son, and called his name Shelah. He was at Chezib when she bore him.
NKJV.6: Then Judah took a wife for Er his firstborn, and her name was Tamar.
NKJV.7: But Er, Judah’s firstborn, was wicked in the sight of the LORD, and the LORD killed him.
NKJV.8: And Judah said to Onan, “Go in to your brother’s wife and marry her, and raise up an heir to your brother.”
NKJV.9: But Onan knew that the heir would not be his; and it came to pass, when he went in to his brother’s wife, that he emitted on the ground, lest he should give an heir to his brother.
NKJV.10: And the thing which he did displeased the LORD; therefore He killed him also.
NKJV.11: Then Judah said to Tamar his daughter-in-law, “Remain a widow in your father’s house till my son Shelah is grown.” For he said, “Lest he also die like his brothers.” And Tamar went and dwelt in her father’s house.
NKJV.12: Now in the process of time the daughter of Shua, Judah’s wife, died; and Judah was comforted, and went up to his sheepshearers at Timnah, he and his friend Hirah the Adullamite.
NKJV.13: And it was told Tamar, saying, “Look, your father-in-law is going up to Timnah to shear his sheep.”
NKJV.14: So she took off her widow’s garments, covered herself with a veil and wrapped herself, and sat in an open place which was on the way to Timnah; for she saw that Shelah was grown, and she was not given to him as a wife.
NKJV.15: When Judah saw her, he thought she was a harlot, because she had covered her face.
NKJV.16: Then he turned to her by the way, and said, “Please let me come in to you”; for he did not know that she was his daughter-in-law. So she said, “What will you give me, that you may come in to me?”
NKJV.17: And he said, “I will send a young goat from the flock.” So she said, “Will you give me a pledge till you send it?”
NKJV.18: Then he said, “What pledge shall I give you?” So she said, “Your signet and cord, and your staff that is in your hand.” Then he gave them to her, and went in to her, and she conceived by him.
NKJV.19: So she arose and went away, and laid aside her veil and put on the garments of her widowhood.
NKJV.20: And Judah sent the young goat by the hand of his friend the Adullamite, to receive his pledge from the woman’s hand, but he did not find her.
NKJV.21: Then he asked the men of that place, saying, “Where is the harlot who was openly by the roadside?” And they said, “There was no harlot in this place.”
NKJV.22: So he returned to Judah and said, “I cannot find her. Also, the men of the place said there was no harlot in this place.”
NKJV.23: Then Judah said, “Let her take them for herself, lest we be shamed; for I sent this young goat and you have not found her.”
NKJV.24: And it came to pass, about three months after, that Judah was told, saying, “Tamar your daughter-in-law has played the harlot; furthermore she is with child by harlotry.” So Judah said, “Bring her out and let her be burned!”
NKJV.25: When she was brought out, she sent to her father-in-law, saying, “By the man to whom these belong, I am with child.” And she said, “Please determine whose these are—the signet and cord, and staff.”
NKJV.26: So Judah acknowledged them and said, “She has been more righteous than I, because I did not give her to Shelah my son.” And he never knew her again.
NKJV.27: Now it came to pass, at the time for giving birth, that behold, twins were in her womb.
NKJV.28: And so it was, when she was giving birth, that the one put out his hand; and the midwife took a scarlet thread and bound it on his hand, saying, “This one came out first.”
NKJV.29: Then it happened, as he drew back his hand, that his brother came out unexpectedly; and she said, “How did you break through? This breach be upon you!” Therefore his name was called Perez.
NKJV.30: Afterward his brother came out who had the scarlet thread on his hand. And his name was called Zerah.

NASB.1: And it came about at that time, that Judah departed from his brothers and visited a certain Adullamite, whose name was Hirah.
NASB.2: Judah saw there a daughter of a certain Canaanite whose name was Shua; and he took her and went in to her.
NASB.3: So she conceived and bore a son and he named him Er.
NASB.4: Then she conceived again and bore a son and named him Onan.
NASB.5: She bore still another son and named him Shelah; and it was at Chezib that she bore him.
NASB.6: Now Judah took a wife for Er his firstborn, and her name [was] Tamar.
NASB.7: But Er, Judah's firstborn, was evil in the sight of the LORD, so the LORD took his life.
NASB.8: Then Judah said to Onan, 'Go in to your brother's wife, and perform your duty as a brother-in-law to her, and raise up offspring for your brother.'
NASB.9: Onan knew that the offspring would not be his; so when he went in to his brother's wife, he wasted his seed on the ground in order not to give offspring to his brother.
NASB.10: But what he did was displeasing in the sight of the LORD; so He took his life also.
NASB.11: Then Judah said to his daughter-in-law Tamar, 'Remain a widow in your father's house until my son Shelah grows up'; for he thought, '[I am afraid] that he too may die like his brothers.' So Tamar went and lived in her father's house.
NASB.12: Now after a considerable time Shua's daughter, the wife of Judah, died; and when the time of mourning was ended, Judah went up to his sheepshearers at Timnah, he and his friend Hirah the Adullamite.
NASB.13: It was told to Tamar, 'Behold, your father-in-law is going up to Timnah to shear his sheep.'
NASB.14: So she removed her widow's garments and covered [herself] with a veil, and wrapped herself, and sat in the gateway of Enaim, which is on the road to Timnah; for she saw that Shelah had grown up, and she had not been given to him as a wife.
NASB.15: When Judah saw her, he thought she [was] a harlot, for she had covered her face.
NASB.16: So he turned aside to her by the road, and said, 'Here now, let me come in to you'; for he did not know that she was his daughter-in-law. And she said, 'What will you give me, that you may come in to me?'
NASB.17: He said, therefore, 'I will send you a young goat from the flock.' She said, moreover, 'Will you give a pledge until you send [it]?'
NASB.18: He said, 'What pledge shall I give you?' And she said, 'Your seal and your cord, and your staff that is in your hand.' So he gave [them] to her and went in to her, and she conceived by him.
NASB.19: Then she arose and departed, and removed her veil and put on her widow's garments.
NASB.20: When Judah sent the young goat by his friend the Adullamite, to receive the pledge from the woman's hand, he did not find her.
NASB.21: He asked the men of her place, saying, 'Where is the temple prostitute who was by the road at Enaim?' But they said, 'There has been no temple prostitute here.'
NASB.22: So he returned to Judah, and said, 'I did not find her; and furthermore, the men of the place said, 'There has been no temple prostitute here.''
NASB.23: Then Judah said, 'Let her keep them, otherwise we will become a laughingstock. After all, I sent this young goat, but you did not find her.'
NASB.24: Now it was about three months later that Judah was informed, 'Your daughter-in-law Tamar has played the harlot, and behold, she is also with child by harlotry.' Then Judah said, 'Bring her out and let her be burned!'
NASB.25: It was while she was being brought out that she sent to her father-in-law, saying, 'I am with child by the man to whom these things belong.' And she said, 'Please examine and see, whose signet ring and cords and staff are these?'
NASB.26: Judah recognized [them], and said, 'She is more righteous than I, inasmuch as I did not give her to my son Shelah.' And he did not have relations with her again.
NASB.27: It came about at the time she was giving birth, that behold, there were twins in her womb.
NASB.28: Moreover, it took place while she was giving birth, one put out a hand, and the midwife took and tied a scarlet [thread] on his hand, saying, 'This one came out first.'
NASB.29: But it came about as he drew back his hand, that behold, his brother came out. Then she said, 'What a breach you have made for yourself!' So he was named Perez.
NASB.30: Afterward his brother came out who had the scarlet [thread] on his hand; and he was named Zerah.

ESV.1: It happened at that time that Judah went down from his brothers and turned aside to a certain Adullamite, whose name was Hirah.
ESV.2: There Judah saw the daughter of a certain Canaanite whose name was Shua. He took her and went in to her,
ESV.3: and she conceived and bore a son, and he called his name Er.
ESV.4: She conceived again and bore a son, and she called his name Onan.
ESV.5: Yet again she bore a son, and she called his name Shelah. Judah  was in Chezib when she bore him.
ESV.6: And Judah took a wife for Er his firstborn, and her name was Tamar.
ESV.7: But Er, Judah's firstborn, was wicked in the sight of the LORD, and the LORD put him to death.
ESV.8: Then Judah said to Onan, “Go in to your brother's wife and perform the duty of a brother-in-law to her, and raise up offspring for your brother.”
ESV.9: But Onan knew that the offspring would not be his. So whenever he went in to his brother's wife he would waste the semen on the ground, so as not to give offspring to his brother.
ESV.10: And what he did was wicked in the sight of the LORD, and he put him to death also.
ESV.11: Then Judah said to Tamar his daughter-in-law, “Remain a widow in your father's house, till Shelah my son grows up” — for he feared that he would die, like his brothers. So Tamar went and remained in her father's house.
ESV.12: In the course of time the wife of Judah, Shua's daughter, died. When Judah was comforted, he went up to Timnah to his sheepshearers, he and his friend Hirah the Adullamite.
ESV.13: And when Tamar was told, “Your father-in-law is going up to Timnah to shear his sheep,”
ESV.14: she took off her widow's garments and covered herself with a veil, wrapping herself up, and sat at the entrance to Enaim, which is on the road to Timnah. For she saw that Shelah was grown up, and she had not been given to him in marriage.
ESV.15: When Judah saw her, he thought she was a prostitute, for she had covered her face.
ESV.16: He turned to her at the roadside and said, “Come, let me come in to you,” for he did not know that she was his daughter-in-law. She said, “What will you give me, that you may come in to me?”
ESV.17: He answered, “I will send you a young goat from the flock.” And she said, “If you give me a pledge, until you send it — ”
ESV.18: He said, “What pledge shall I give you?” She replied, “Your signet and your cord and your staff that is in your hand.” So he gave them to her and went in to her, and she conceived by him.
ESV.19: Then she arose and went away, and taking off her veil she put on the garments of her widowhood.
ESV.20: When Judah sent the young goat by his friend the Adullamite to take back the pledge from the woman's hand, he did not find her.
ESV.21: And he asked the men of the place, “Where is the cult prostitute  who was at Enaim at the roadside?” And they said, “No cult prostitute has been here.”
ESV.22: So he returned to Judah and said, “I have not found her. Also, the men of the place said, ‘No cult prostitute has been here.’”
ESV.23: And Judah replied, “Let her keep the things as her own, or we shall be laughed at. You see, I sent this young goat, and you did not find her.”
ESV.24: About three months later Judah was told, “Tamar your daughter-in-law has been immoral.  Moreover, she is pregnant by immorality.”  And Judah said, “Bring her out, and let her be burned.”
ESV.25: As she was being brought out, she sent word to her father-in-law, “By the man to whom these belong, I am pregnant.” And she said, “Please identify whose these are, the signet and the cord and the staff.”
ESV.26: Then Judah identified them and said, “She is more righteous than I, since I did not give her to my son Shelah.” And he did not know her again.
ESV.27: When the time of her labor came, there were twins in her womb.
ESV.28: And when she was in labor, one put out a hand, and the midwife took and tied a scarlet thread on his hand, saying, “This one came out first.”
ESV.29: But as he drew back his hand, behold, his brother came out. And she said, “What a breach you have made for yourself!” Therefore his name was called Perez.
ESV.30: Afterward his brother came out with the scarlet thread on his hand, and his name was called Zerah.

NLT.1: About this time, Judah left home and moved to Adullam, where he stayed with a man named Hirah.
NLT.2: There he saw a Canaanite woman, the daughter of Shua, and he married her. When he slept with her,
NLT.3: she became pregnant and gave birth to a son, and he named the boy Er.
NLT.4: Then she became pregnant again and gave birth to another son, and she named him Onan.
NLT.5: And when she gave birth to a third son, she named him Shelah. At the time of Shelah’s birth, they were living at Kezib.
NLT.6: In the course of time, Judah arranged for his firstborn son, Er, to marry a young woman named Tamar.
NLT.7: But Er was a wicked man in the LORD’s sight, so the LORD took his life.
NLT.8: Then Judah said to Er’s brother Onan, “Go and marry Tamar, as our law requires of the brother of a man who has died. You must produce an heir for your brother.”
NLT.9: But Onan was not willing to have a child who would not be his own heir. So whenever he had intercourse with his brother’s wife, he spilled the semen on the ground. This prevented her from having a child who would belong to his brother.
NLT.10: But the LORD considered it evil for Onan to deny a child to his dead brother. So the LORD took Onan’s life, too.
NLT.11: Then Judah said to Tamar, his daughter-in-law, “Go back to your parents’ home and remain a widow until my son Shelah is old enough to marry you.” (But Judah didn’t really intend to do this because he was afraid Shelah would also die, like his two brothers.) So Tamar went back to live in her father’s home.
NLT.12: Some years later Judah’s wife died. After the time of mourning was over, Judah and his friend Hirah the Adullamite went up to Timnah to supervise the shearing of his sheep.
NLT.13: Someone told Tamar, “Look, your father-in-law is going up to Timnah to shear his sheep.”
NLT.14: Tamar was aware that Shelah had grown up, but no arrangements had been made for her to come and marry him. So she changed out of her widow’s clothing and covered herself with a veil to disguise herself. Then she sat beside the road at the entrance to the village of Enaim, which is on the road to Timnah.
NLT.15: Judah noticed her and thought she was a prostitute, since she had covered her face.
NLT.16: So he stopped and propositioned her. “Let me have sex with you,” he said, not realizing that she was his own daughter-in-law. “How much will you pay to have sex with me?” Tamar asked.
NLT.17: “I’ll send you a young goat from my flock,” Judah promised. “But what will you give me to guarantee that you will send the goat?” she asked.
NLT.18: “What kind of guarantee do you want?” he replied. She answered, “Leave me your identification seal and its cord and the walking stick you are carrying.” So Judah gave them to her. Then he had intercourse with her, and she became pregnant.

WEB.1: At that time, Judah went down from his brothers, and visited a certain Adullamite, whose name was Hirah.

AMP.1: Now at that time, Judah left his brothers and went down to [stay with] a certain Adullamite named Hirah.
AMP.2: There Judah saw a daughter of Shua, a Canaanite, and he took her [as his wife] and lived with her.
AMP.3: So she conceived and gave birth to a son and Judah named him Er.
AMP.4: Then she conceived again and gave birth to a son and named him Onan.
AMP.5: Again she conceived and gave birth to still another son and named him Shelah. It was at Chezib that she gave birth to him.
AMP.6: Now Judah took a wife for Er his firstborn; her name was Tamar.
AMP.7: But Er, Judah's firstborn, was evil in the sight of the LORD, and the LORD killed him [in judgment].
AMP.8: Then Judah told Onan, "Go in to your brother's widow, and perform your duty as a brother-in-law [under the levirate marriage custom]; [be her husband and] raise children for [the name of] your brother."
AMP.9: Onan knew that the child (heir) would not be his [but his dead brother's]; so whenever he lay with his brother's widow, he spilled his seed on the ground [to prevent conception], so that he would not give a child to his brother.
AMP.10: But what he did was displeasing in the sight of the LORD; therefore He killed him also [in judgment].
AMP.11: Then Judah said to Tamar, his daughter-in-law, "Remain a widow at your father's house until Shelah my [youngest] son is grown"; [but he was deceiving her] for he thought that [if Shelah should marry her] he too might die like his brothers did. So Tamar went and lived in her father's house.
AMP.12: But quite a while later, Judah's wife, the daughter of Shua, died; and when the time of mourning was ended, he went up to his sheepshearers at Timnah with his friend Hirah the Adullamite.
AMP.13: Tamar was told, "Listen, your father-in-law is going up to Timnah to shear his sheep."
AMP.14: So she removed her widow's clothes and covered herself with a veil, and wrapped herself up [in disguise], and sat in the gateway of Enaim, which is on the road to Timnah; for she saw that Shelah had grown up, and she had not been given to him as a wife [as Judah had promised].
AMP.15: When Judah saw her, he thought she was a [temple] prostitute, for she had covered her face [as such women did].
AMP.16: He turned to her by the road, and said, "Please come, let me lie with you"; for he did not know that she was his daughter-in-law. And she said, "What will you give me, that you may lie with me?"
AMP.17: He answered, "I will send you a young goat from the flock." And she said, "Will you give me a pledge [as a deposit] until you send it?"
AMP.18: He said, "What pledge shall I give you?" She said, "Your seal and your cord, and the staff that is in your hand." So he gave them to her and was intimate with her, and she conceived by him.
AMP.19: Then she got up and left, and removed her veil and put on her widow's clothing.
AMP.20: When Judah sent the young goat by his friend the Adullamite, to get his pledge [back] from the woman, he was unable to find her.
AMP.21: He asked the men of that place, "Where is the temple prostitute who was by the roadside at Enaim?" They said, "There was no prostitute here."
AMP.22: So he returned to Judah, and said, "I cannot find her; also the local men said, 'There was no prostitute around here.'"
AMP.23: Then Judah said, "Let her keep the things (pledge articles) for herself, otherwise we will be a laughingstock [searching everywhere for her]. After all, I sent this young goat, but you did not find her."
AMP.24: About three months later Judah was told, "Tamar your daughter-in-law has played the [role of a] prostitute, and she is with child because of her immorality." So Judah said, "Bring her out and let her be burned [to death as punishment]!"
AMP.25: While she was being brought out, she [took the things Judah had given her and] sent [them along with a message] to her father-in-law, saying, "I am with child by the man to whom these articles belong." And she added, "Please examine [them carefully] and see [clearly] to whom these things belong, the seal and the cord and staff."
AMP.26: Judah recognized the articles, and said, "She has been more righteous [in this matter] than I, because I did not give her to my son Shelah [as I had promised]." And Judah did not have [intimate] relations with her again.
AMP.27: Now when the time came for her to give birth, there were twins in her womb.
AMP.28: And when she was in labor, one [baby] put out his hand, and the midwife took his hand and tied a scarlet thread on it, saying, "This one was born first."
AMP.29: But he pulled back his hand, and his brother was born first. And she said, "What a breach you have made for yourself [to be the firstborn]!" So he was named Perez (breach, break forth).
AMP.30: Afterward his brother who had the scarlet [thread] on his hand was born and was named Zerah (brightness).

NIV.26: Judah recognized them and said, “She is more righteous than I, since I wouldn’t give her to my son Shelah.” And he did not sleep with her again.
NIV.27: When the time came for her to give birth, there were twin boys in her womb.
NIV.28: As she was giving birth, one of them put out his hand; so the midwife took a scarlet thread and tied it on his wrist and said, “This one came out first.”
NIV.29: But when he drew back his hand, his brother came out, and she said, “So this is how you have broken out!” And he was named Perez.
NIV.30: Then his brother, who had the scarlet thread on his wrist, came out and he was given the name Zerah.

MSG.1: About that time, Judah separated from his brothers and hooked up with a man in Adullam named Hirah.
MSG.2: While there, Judah met the daughter of a Canaanite named Shua. He married her, they went to bed,
MSG.3: she became pregnant and had a son named Er.
MSG.4: She got pregnant again and had a son named Onan.
MSG.5: She had still another son; she named this one Shelah. They were living at Kezib when she had him.
MSG.6: Judah got a wife for Er, his firstborn. Her name was Tamar.
MSG.7: But Judah's firstborn, Er, grievously offended God and God took his life.
MSG.8: So Judah told Onan, "Go and sleep with your brother's widow; it's the duty of a brother-in-law to keep your brother's line alive."
MSG.9: But Onan knew that the child wouldn't be his, so whenever he slept with his brother's widow he spilled his semen on the ground so he wouldn't produce a child for his brother.
MSG.10: God was much offended by what he did and also took his life.
MSG.11: So Judah stepped in and told his daughter-in-law Tamar, "Live as a widow at home with your father until my son Shelah grows up." He was worried that Shelah would also end up dead, just like his brothers. So Tamar went to live with her father.
MSG.12: Time passed. Judah's wife, Shua's daughter, died. When the time of mourning was over, Judah with his friend Hirah of Adullam went to Timnah for the sheep shearing.
MSG.13: Tamar was told, "Your father-in-law has gone to Timnah to shear his sheep."
MSG.14: She took off her widow's clothes, put on a veil to disguise herself, and sat at the entrance to Enaim which is on the road to Timnah. She realized by now that even though Shelah was grown up, she wasn't going to be married to him.
MSG.15: Judah saw her and assumed she was a prostitute since she had veiled her face.
MSG.16:
He left the road and went over to her. He said, "Let me sleep with you." He had no idea that she was his daughter-in-law.
She said, "What will you pay me?"
MSG.17:
"I'll send you," he said, "a kid goat from the flock."
She said, "Not unless you give me a pledge until you send it."
MSG.18:
"So what would you want in the way of a pledge?"
She said, "Your personal seal-and-cord and the staff you carry."
He handed them over to her and slept with her. And she got pregnant.
MSG.19: She then left and went home. She removed her veil and put her widow's clothes back on.
MSG.20: Judah sent the kid goat by his friend from Adullam to recover the pledge from the woman. But he couldn't find her.
MSG.21:
He asked the men of that place, "Where's the prostitute that used to sit by the road here near Enaim?"
They said, "There's never been a prostitute here."
MSG.22: He went back to Judah and said, "I couldn't find her. The men there said there never has been a prostitute there."
MSG.23: Judah said, "Let her have it then. If we keep looking, everyone will be poking fun at us. I kept my part of the bargain—I sent the kid goat but you couldn't find her."
MSG.24:
Three months or so later, Judah was told, "Your daughter-in-law has been playing the whore—and now she's a pregnant whore."
Judah yelled, "Get her out here. Burn her up!"
MSG.25: As they brought her out, she sent a message to her father-in-law, "I'm pregnant by the man who owns these things. Identify them, please. Who's the owner of the seal-and-cord and the staff?"
MSG.26: Judah saw they were his. He said, "She's in the right; I'm in the wrong—I wouldn't let her marry my son Shelah." He never slept with her again.
MSG.27: When her time came to give birth, it turned out that there were twins in her womb.
MSG.28: As she was giving birth, one put his hand out; the midwife tied a red thread on his hand, saying, "This one came first."
MSG.29: But then he pulled it back and his brother came out. She said, "Oh! A breakout!" So she named him Perez (Breakout).
MSG.30: Then his brother came out with the red thread on his hand. They named him Zerah (Bright).
